newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea, European AIR in mid-sized plane venture.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea, European AIR in mid-sized plane venture.

text.p: A South Korean consortium of aerospace companies and a European consortium, Aero International Regional (AIR), have agreed to jointly develop medium-sized passenger planes, Seoul's trade ministry said on Friday.

The Korean Commercial Aircraft Development Consortium and AIR are due to sign a memorandum of understanding later on Friday in Seoul on a $1.2 billion project to make 70-seater and other similar passenger planes from 2001, the ministry said.

The South Korean consortium is led by Samsung Aerospace Industries Co, while AIR is equally owned by France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc and Italy's Alenia, an official at the South Korean consortium said.
The South Korean consortium also includes 13 other firms, including Korean Air Lines Co, Daewoo Heavy Industries Co and Hyundai Space and Aircraft Co.
South Korean firms will hold a stake of at least 30 percent in the project and a final contract is scheduled to be made within three months, the ministry statement said.
Airplane assembly will be done by AIR or its member companies, while South Korea will be in charge of aircraft completion work and delivery to Asian customers.

Earlier talks between South Korea and China on forming a joint venture to develop medium-sized passenger planes fell apart. South Korean talks on taking over stricken Dutch plane maker Fokker also failed to produce results.
